sources.news_title: BigXthaPlug Arrested on Drug and Gun Charges in Texas While Already on Bail From 'A Year Ago'
sources.text:
BigXthaPlug Arrested on Drug and Gun Charges in Texas While Already on Bail From 'A Year Ago'
A breakout Dallas rapper finds his biggest momentum colliding head-on with a growing stack of weapon and drug cases
Dallas rapper BigXthaPlug was arrested in Texas on Friday on suspicion of driving while intoxicated, marijuana possession and unlawful possession of a firearm, according to Allen County Police. The 28-year-old artist, real name Xavier Landum, was taken into custody in Allen and booked into Collin County Jail before later being released.
The latest arrest comes while BigXthaPlug is already on bail over similar allegations from about a year ago. In August 2024, police records show he was arrested on charges of unlawful possession of a weapon and a small amount of marijuana, a case that remains active. Court documents also indicate he faced comparable charges in 2022, suggesting a pattern that prosecutors are unlikely to ignore.
Police in Allen, north of Dallas, told BBC Newsbeat that officers stopped the musician on Friday and subsequently arrested him on suspicion of driving while intoxicated, drug possession and illegal firearm possession. No further details of the stop, such as the quantity of marijuana allegedly found or the type of weapon involved, have been made public.
A spokesperson for Allen County Police said officers followed standard procedure and transferred Landum to Collin County Jail shortly after the arrest. Jail records confirmed he was later released, although the terms of that release, including any bond conditions or travel restrictions, have not been disclosed.
Bigxthaplug's Rising Profile and a Career in Flux
The news landed at a particularly awkward moment for BigXthaPlug, who has been edging from regional cult favourite to mainstream recognition over the past two years.
The Dallas rapper built his name on a hybrid sound that pulls from southern hip-hop, trap and country-rap, and he broke through with the viral singles Texas, The Largest and Mmhmm, tracks that have circulated heavily on TikTok and rap-focused playlists.
He had recently teased new music on Instagram, telling fans he was gearing up to drop fresh material soon. He was also due to perform at the Country Rising festival on Friday, a booking that underlined how quickly he has climbed festival bills.
Organisers later posted on Instagram that he would no longer be appearing due to what they described as a 'personal emergency.' They did not mention the arrest.
That vague explanation, paired with the sudden cancellation, sparked the usual flood of speculation in fan comment sections. Some followers urged patience and sent support, others were bluntly annoyed at buying tickets for a set that evaporated hours before showtime. None of this is unusual in the age of always-on fandom, but it shows how fast the narrative around an artist can flip.
Performing Days After Arrest Keeps Bigxthaplug in Spotlight
BigXthaPlug did not retreat from the public eye after his release from jail. Videos shared on social media show him taking the stage at the Iowa State Fair on Saturday as scheduled, only a day after the arrest in Texas. Footage circulated by fans captures him opening his set by telling the crowd: 'They didn't think I was coming.'
That line drew loud cheers, and it also doubled as a not-so-subtle nod to the drama surrounding his absence from Country Rising. It was the kind of moment rappers often lean on, turning legal trouble into fuel for the stage narrative. Whether that plays well with judges and probation officers is another matter entirely.
Fair organisers have not commented publicly on the arrest, and there is no indication from the clips that the performance was cut short or altered. For the thousands in the crowd, it looked like a fairly normal night of music, which is slightly wild considering he had been in a Texas jail cell barely 24 hours earlier.
The latest legal tangle comes after a busy run of live shows. BigXthaPlug performed at Wireless Festival in the UK in 2025, shortly before releasing his most recent album. That slot put him in front of one of Europe's most influential rap crowds and helped broaden his reach beyond the US southern rap circuit.
Legal Clouds Gather Again Over Bigxthaplug
The most serious question now is how Friday's arrest will affect the ongoing case from August last year. At that time, police accused him of unlawful possession of a weapon and a small amount of marijuana. Because that case is still continuing, any fresh allegations may be treated as a potential breach of bail or bond terms.
Local prosecutors have not yet stated whether they will seek to tighten restrictions on the rapper, revoke bail or fold the new allegations into the existing case.
No court hearing dates in connection with Friday's arrest have been made public. Without those filings, key details remain uncertain, including what formal charges will ultimately be laid.
The history stretching back to 2022, when he reportedly faced similar weapon and marijuana allegations, gives the authorities a longer timeline to work with. Defence lawyers often argue that young artists are targeted or over-policed, especially in the US South. Police typically counter that, for them, it is about guns, roadside stops and the law, not streaming numbers.
Allen County Police have not released body camera footage of the arrest or a detailed incident report. Until that happens, the public version of events will be shaped mainly by terse police statements on one side and social media gossip on the other. Nothing is confirmed yet so everything should be taken with a grain of salt.
What is clear is that BigXthaPlug now has three sets of weapon and drug allegations across four years hanging over him just as his career starts to scale up. Promoters, brands and festival bookers tend to look hard at those patterns, whatever fans might say in the comments.
He still has music on the way, if his recent Instagram hints are to be believed. Whether that roll-out goes to plan, or ends up threading around court dates and bond hearings, is now very much an open question.

sources.news_title: BigXthaPlug arrested on drug and gun charges in Texas
sources.text:
BigXthaPlug was arrested on drug and gun charges in Texas, causing him to miss a scheduled performance at a music festival.
The country rapper, real name Xavier Landum, was arrested on Friday (August 21), the same day he was due to perform at Manitoba’s Country Rising Festival.
Landum was pulled over by the Allen Police Department and booked into the Collin County Jail on charges of driving while intoxicated, marijuana possession of less than 2 ounces, and unlawful possession of a firearm, per NBC.
He was on bail at the time of his arrest, following an arrest exactly one year ago for marijuana possession and unlawful possession of a firearm in Dallas. Organisers of Manitoba’s Country Rising Festival have said they understood fans’ “disappointment and frustration” by the rapper’s absence due to a “personal emergency.”
The Winnipeg Goldeyes Baseball Club, where the festival is held, said they “share the disappointment and frustration felt by those in attendance,” but noted they were “serving as the host venue only” and “not responsible for the event’s programming, artist bookings, scheduling or related decisions.”
— Winnipeg Goldeyes (@Wpg_Goldeyes) August 21, 2026
Despite the arrest, BigXthaPlug still performed last night (August 22) at the Iowa State Fair Grandstand. Shortly before his scheduled slot, he shared an Instagram story where he told fans, “I’m on my way.”
Recommended
Later, he shared an Instagram post with a thumbnail of his mugshot, teasing his upcoming album with a clip of a new track.
BigXthaPlug rose to prominence in 2023 for his hits ‘Texas’ and ‘Mmhmm’, the former of which was part of his debut album ‘Amar’, written while he was in solitary confinement in jail for illegal possession of weapons and marijuana in 2022.
The rapper performed at Wireless Festival in 2025, shortly before releasing his latest and third album, ‘I Hope You’re Happy’. Before that, in 2024, he shared his second album ‘Take Care’.

sources.news_title: BigXThaPlug arrested in Texas less than 24 hours before Iowa State Fair concert
sources.text:
BigXThaPlug arrested in Texas less than 24 hours before Iowa State Fair concert, but officials say he will still perform
Related coverage in the video above: Nebraska State Fair headliner
The headliner for the Iowa State Fair Grandstand show Saturday has been arrested in Texas, but fair officials say they have been told he will make it for the show.
BigXThaPlug, the stage name of Xavier Landum, is facing driving while intoxicated, marijuana possession and illegal firearm possession charges. Landum was booked into Collin County Jail Friday night. Landum was jailed on drug and weapons charges in 2022 and 2025.
This arrest came less than 24 hours before the hip-hop and rap artist is set to headline the Iowa State Fair Grandstand with special guest XOLEX.
KCCI did reach out to the Iowa State Fair late Friday night regarding whether the show would be impacted by Landum's arrest. Fair officials sent a statement saying, "We are aware of reports regarding BigXthaPlug. We are in communication with his agent and at this time, we have been told he will still be performing."
Around noon Saturday, the rapper posted a short video on his Instagram story saying, "Des Moines, Iowa, I'm on my way."
Last week, Rod Stewart was set to play on the first Friday of the fair but bowed out two days before for medical reasons. The Iowa State Fair refunded people who bought tickets for Stewart's show. John Waite was booked in Stewart's place, and the show was free for fairgoers.

sources.news_title: BigXthaPlug Faces Drug and Gun Charges One Year After Last Arrest
sources.text:
Trending on Billboard
BigXthaPlug has had another run-in with the law.
Exactly one year after his previous arrest on similar charges, the 28-year-old rapper was arrested again in Texas on Friday (Aug. 21).
The Dallas native, whose real name is Xavier Landum, was arrested by the Allen Police Department and booked into Collin County Jail on charges of driving while intoxicated, possession of less than 2 ounces of marijuana and unlawful possession of a firearm, according to Dallas’ KDFW.
On Aug. 21, 2025, BigXthaPlug was arrested in North Texas on marijuana and weapon possession charges. He was out on bail for those charges when he was arrested Friday.
The rapper was scheduled to perform at the Country Rising Festival in Winnipeg, Manitoba, but was forced to cancel his appearance.
Organizers wrote in a statement on X that they understood the “disappointment and frustrated felt by those in attendance.” In another statement on Instagram, the festival wrote that BigXthaPlug wouldn’t be appearing “due to a personal emergency.”
The rapper is still slated to perform at the Iowa State Fair Grandstand on Saturday (Aug. 22). “We are aware of reports regarding BigXthaPlug. We are in communication with his agent and at this time, we have been told he will still be performing,” organizers there told KCCI in Des Moines.
In February 2025, BigXthaPlug was arrested on a marijuana possession charge in Arlington, Texas.
Last September, BigXthaPlug earned his first No. 1 on Billboard’s Hot Rap Songs chart with “All the Way,” featuring Bailey Zimmerman. Its parent album, I Hope You’re Happy, debuted in the top two on both the Top Rap Albums and Top Country Albums charts.

One of the biggest rappers working today finds himself in some hot water. News in Dallas and Fort Worth reported BigXthaPlug getting arrested by local authorities. He was charged with driving while intoxicated, marijuana possession, and unlawful possession of a firearm. Currently, there are no additional details that lend context to what led to his arrest.
We do know that he was slated to perform at the Country Rising Festival on the same day he got arrested. The rapper born Xavier Darnell Landum pulled out due to a “personal emergency.”
Videos by VICE

sources.news_title: BigXthaPlug arrested, still scheduled to perform at Iowa State Fair grandstand Saturday
BigXthaPlug's Iowa State Fair show to go on despite arrest in Texas
sources.text:
BigXthaPlug's Iowa State Fair show goes on despite arrest in Texas
BigXthaPlug's Grandstand show at the Iowa State Fair went on despite his arrest and jailing in Texas.
The show wrapped up around 10 p.m. after the artist rushed to Iowa to keep his headlining concert date Saturday, Aug. 22, despite his arrest Friday in the Dallas suburb of Allen.
He was arrested on charges of driving while intoxicated, possession of marijuana and unlicensed possession of a firearm, according to Collin County, Texas jail records.
KXAS-TV, a Fort Worth, Texas, NBC affiliate, reported that BigXthaPlug, whose legal name is Xavier Landum, had previous similar arrests in Texas in 2025.
The fair previously had a cancellation by Aug. 14 Grandstand headliner Rod Stewart, who cited medical reasons. It provided refunds and arranged for John Waite to perform a free Grandstand show in Stewart's place, which drew about 2,000 people.
Prior to Stewart's cancellation, the fair had been on course to beat last year's record number of Grandstand tickets sold. Despite falling short of that goal, the fair still beat the single show ticket record with Lainey Wilson's sold-out show on Sunday, Aug. 16.
BigXthaPlug, of Dallas, is known for his mix of rap and country alongside big-name country artists like Luke Combs, Ella Langley, Bailey Zimmerman, Jelly Roll and Darius Rucker. His hits include "Texas" and "Mmhmm."
"Hip-hop and country music both have the same base, which is storytelling," he told The New York Times in an interview.

sources.text:
Audio By Carbonatix

sources.news_title: Dallas rapper BigXthaPlug arrested, nearly a year after being taken into custody before album release, police say
sources.text:
Dallas rapper BigXthaPlug arrested, nearly a year after being taken into custody before album release, police say
Dallas rapper BigXthaPlug was arrested Friday, nearly a year after police took him into custody ahead of his 2025 album release, authorities said.
Born Xavier Landum, BigXthaPlug is facing driving while intoxicated, possession of marijuana, and illegal possession of a firearm charges, according to the Allen Police Department.
He was booked into Collin County Jail.
"At this time, we can confirm that an arrest has been made," said Sam Rippamonti, public information officer for Allen police. "However, we are unable to provide any additional details."
The investigation remains active, Rippamonti said.
In late August 2025, BigXthaPlug was jailed on drug and weapons charges.
At that time, Dallas police said officers pulled over a pickup truck missing its front license plate on South Great Trinity Forest Way near U.S. 175. An officer asked the driver, identified as Landum, if he had a firearm. BigXthaPlug told officers he did and detailed where to find it in the truck. Police said a criminal database flagged Landum as connected to a gang in Arlington, which meant he was not legally allowed to possess a gun.
Police said they also found a small amount of marijuana in the truck.
Before his 2025 arrest, BigXthaPlug had been scheduled to appear at an album release party in Deep Ellum to celebrate his then-new album, I Hope You're Happy. The album included songs with artists such as Darius Rucker, Luke Combs, Shaboozey, and Jelly Roll.
BigXthaPlug was born in Dallas and has lived in North Texas. His hit songs include "Texas" and "Mmhmm." He had also previously been arrested on drug and weapons charges in 2022.
CBS News Texas will provide updates as more information becomes available.

sources.news_title: Rapper BigXthaPlug Misses Headlining Appearance At Country Festival After Being Arrested Earlier In The Day
sources.text:
Hard to get to Canada when you’re in jail in Dallas.
Rapper BigXthaPlug missed a headlining performance at a country music festival on Friday after being arrested earlier in the day on a slew of charges in his home state of Texas.
BigXthaPlug, whose real name is Xavier Landum, was arrested early Friday by the Allen Police Department on charges of driving while intoxicated, marijuana possession of less than 2 ounces, and unlawful possession of a firearm, and was taken to the Collin County Jail.
Unfortunately, he was scheduled to headline the Country Rising festival in Winnipeg, Canada later that evening, and was forced to miss his appearance.
The festival made the announcement Friday afternoon, saying that BigX was unable to make it due to a “personal emergency.”
And naturally, fans who had bought tickets specifically to see the Texas rapper weren’t happy about the last-minute cancellation:
“That is brutal! Came specifically for Big X! Where’s the refund?”
“I need the biggest, the largest refund asap”
The arrest, ironically, comes exactly one year after BigX was arrested in Dallas on misdemeanor charges of possession of marijuana less than 2 ounces and unlawful possession of a firearm. That arrest last year came on the same day released his country-inspired album I Hope You’re Happy, which features collabs with several top country artists like Ella Langley, Jelly Roll, Shaboozey, Bailey Zimmerman and Luke Combs.
The Country Rising festival in Winnipeg continued on without their headliner, featuring performances from Corey Kent, Dylan Marlowe and Redferrin, but BigXthaPlug is also scheduled to headline the Iowa State Fair tonight, August 22, which has fans wondering whether he’ll be able to make that appearance.
A search of the Collin County Jail website shows that BigX doesn’t appear to still be behind bars, so maybe he’ll be able to make it to Iowa for tonight’s show.
Let’s just hope he’s not the one driving…
BigXthaPlug Headlined The Ryman Auditorium Last Year
Shaboozey educating other artists on the history of country music.
When it comes to historical venues in country music, there’s nowhere more important to the genre than the Ryman Auditorium.
Step inside the doors and you can feel the history in the building, a landmark that’s hosted the biggest legends in country music on its stage. It’s my favorite building in Nashville, a place that leaves me in awe every time I step inside and see the sun shining through its stained glass windows.
The building was constructed in the late 1800s by Thomas Ryman, a riverboat captain and saloon owner who wanted a place for the famous preacher Sam P. Jones to hold his revivals in Nashville. Named the Union Gospel Tabernacle, the historic building first opened its doors to worshipers in 1892 – before it even had a roof. Total construction costs were around $100,000, or almost $3 million in today’s money, and the Tabernacle held 6,000 people after the addition of a balcony. (The capacity was later reduced to 3,000 after a stage was added).
After Thomas Ryman passed away in 1904, Sam Jones proposed that the building be renamed in Ryman’s honor – something Ryman had resisted when it was first proposed.
The Ryman continued to host religious events after its namesake’s death, but it was also rented out for non-religious events as well so that it could remain open and operating. And one of those events was the Grand Ole Opry.
The Opry had bounced around from venue to venue after starting out in the studios of WSM, the radio station started by the National Life & Accident Insurance Company in an attempt to boost their insurance business. And in 1943, it was asked to leave its current home at the War Memorial Auditorium after rowdy crowds kept damaging the upholstered seats.
So when Opry management went looking for a new home, the Ryman – with its wooden benches that would be safe from destruction – was the perfect home.
The Ryman hosted its first Grand Ole Opry performance on June 5, 1943.
And for the next 31 years, the Opry continued to host the biggest names in all of country music from the Mother Church of Country Music – everyone from Hank Williams and Roy Acuff to Johnny Cash, George Jones and Loretta Lynn. Elvis even made his first – and only – appearance at the Grand Ole Opry on the stage of the Ryman Auditorium.
The Opry moved to its new home in 1974, leaving the Ryman largely vacant for the next two decades. There were plans to tear the building down, something that was even supported by Roy Acuff. But critics fiercely opposed its destruction, and the Ryman was ultimately spared from the wrecking ball.
A new chapter for the Ryman started in 1991, when Emmylou Harris used the then-dilapidated building to record a live album, which reignited interest in the historic stage. The Ryman was renovated (at the time Harris recorded her album, audience members couldn’t even sit under the balcony, which limited the capacity to about 200 people), and the Ryman reopened in 1994, serving as the centerpiece of entertainment in downtown Nashville.
It’s impossible to name all of the legends who have performed at the “Mother Church of Country Music” in its history, from Hank Williams and Johnny Cash to Aretha Franklin and Louis Armstrong. It’s been memorialized in songs and recordings, and was officially designated a National Historic Landmark in 2001.
But before he performed there, BigXthaPlug wasn’t aware of the history inside the walls of the old church.
The Dallas, Texas native performed a sold-out show at the Ryman for Apple Music Live back on October 1, 2025. Leading up to the show, however, BigX admits that it wasn’t until a conversation with Shaboozey that he realized how much it meant to play the Ryman.
During a conversation with Ebro Darden for Apple Music Live, the rapper was asked whether he understood the magnitude of performing at the iconic venue.
“I wasn’t until last night.”
BigX says that he had attended Shaboozey’s show at The Pinnacle in Nashville, and couldn’t understand why the “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” singer was impressed that he was headlining the Ryman:
“Shaboozey had a show last night. I went to it and after the show we was talking and he was like, ‘Man, you performing at the Ryman, man. That’s crazy.’ I’m like, ‘You didn’t just see what you just performed here? THIS was crazy.’
He like, ‘Nah, bro. It’s like, it’s historical. Do you know the history behind it?’ I’m like, ‘Nah.’ He like, ‘Man, it’s this old church…’ He just gave me the whole rundown. And by the end of it I was like, man, I’m doing something that you can tell the greats do, you know what I’m saying what?
The fact that, like I said, I was chose to step on a stage that greats have been on and a place that’s not my home, but that’s accepting me. You know what I’m saying? So, it’s just crazy.”
While Shaboozey may get some criticism for his music not being “traditional” country, I’ve always respected the way he knows and appreciates the history of the genre, so it’s good to see that he’s educating other artists on it too.

BigXthaPlug Arrested On DWI & G*n Charges After Missing Festival Performance Due To ‘Personal Emergency’
Dallas rapper BigXthaPlug is facing multiple charges following his latest arrest in Texas.
The 27-year-old rapper, whose real name is Xavier Landum, was arrested by Allen police on Friday (Aug. 21) and booked into the Collin County Jail. According to jail records, BigXthaPlug was charged with driving while intoxicated, possession of less than two ounces of marijuana, and unlawful possession of a fire@rm. Authorities have not released details surrounding what allegedly led to the arrest.
BigXthaPlug was scheduled to perform at the Country Rising Festival that same day but missed his appearance. Festival organizers reportedly told fans that the rapper was unable to perform due to a “personal emergency.”
Interestingly, the arrest came exactly one year after BigXthaPlug was arrested in Dallas on Aug. 21, 2025, for marijuana possession and unlawful possession of a f!rearm. That arrest happened on the same day he released his album I Hope You’re Happy. He was also arrested in Arlington in February 2025 for marijuana possession, though that case was later dismissed.
BigXthaPlug has become one of Dallas’ biggest breakout rap stars in recent years. After beginning his music career in 2023, he gained widespread attention with his single “Texas” and later launched his own record label. sources.news_title: BigXthaPlug Arrested in North Texas on DWI, Marijuana and Firearm Charges
sources.text:
BigXthaPlug Arrested in North Texas on DWI, Marijuana and Firearm Charges
| Dallas rapper BigXthaPlug, whose legal name is Xavier Landum, is shown in a Feb. 26, 2025, booking photo released by the Arlington Police Department following a separate marijuana-possession arrest. Landum was arrested again Aug. 21, 2026, by Allen police and booked into the Collin County Jail on DWI, marijuana and firearm charges. (Arlington Police Department, file) | 
The Dallas rapper, whose legal name is Xavier Landum, was arrested Friday by Allen police and booked into the Collin County Jail.
Jail records list three charges: driving while intoxicated, possession of less than 2 ounces of marijuana and unlawful possession of a firearm.
What led to those charges has not been made public.
Allen Police Department spokesperson Sam Rippamonti confirmed the arrest Friday evening and said the investigation remains active. The department declined to provide additional details.
No publicly available account reviewed Friday explained where the arrest occurred, what prompted officers to encounter Landum or the evidence underlying the DWI and firearm allegations.
The charges are accusations. Landum has not been convicted in connection with Friday’s arrest.
The date adds an unusual wrinkle to his latest legal trouble.
Landum was also arrested Aug. 21, 2025, after Dallas police stopped his pickup truck on Great Trinity Forest Way because it did not have a front license plate.
Police said they found marijuana and firearms in the vehicle.
Dallas County records show Landum was booked early the following morning on charges of possession of less than 2 ounces of marijuana and unlawful possession of a firearm. He was later released after posting $5,000 bond.
That arrest came on the eve of the Aug. 22 release of “I Hope You’re Happy,” the album that accelerated BigXthaPlug’s push beyond Southern rap and into country music.
The project paired him with artists including Darius Rucker, Jelly Roll, Bailey Zimmerman, Luke Combs, Shaboozey, Ella Langley and Thomas Rhett.
Friday’s arrest also coincided with a canceled performance several hundred miles away.
BigXthaPlug had been scheduled to perform Friday at Country Rising Festival in Winnipeg, Manitoba.
The festival announced on its official website that he would not appear because of a “personal emergency.”
Country Rising did not identify the emergency or say that Landum’s arrest was the reason for his absence.
The show continued without him.
He is booked to headline the Iowa State Fair Grandstand in Des Moines at 8 p.m. Saturday, Aug. 22, with XOLEX as the special guest.
As of late Friday, the fair’s official website still listed BigXthaPlug as the headliner and continued to offer tickets for the concert. No cancellation or lineup change had been announced.
The Iowa date comes during a period in which BigXthaPlug has pushed well beyond the Southern rap audience that first made him a breakout act. His 2024 album “Take Care” debuted at No. 8 on the Billboard 200, while “I Hope You’re Happy” debuted at No. 7 and further developed the country-rap crossover that has become a major part of his recent work.
“All the Way,” his collaboration with Bailey Zimmerman, reached No. 1 on both Billboard’s Hot Rap Songs and Hot Country Songs charts — an unusual overlap reflected in a State Fair booking that pairs the Dallas rapper with Iowa-born country artist XOLEX.
